# Gemini in Google Sheets Is Now on iOS — Here's What It Does

> **In short:** Google's Gemini AI helper has arrived in Google Sheets on iOS, letting you ask plain-language questions about your data and generate charts from your phone. The gradual rollout started on October 15, 2026, and the feature is available across Workspace, Education, and paid consumer AI plans.

You've probably opened a spreadsheet on your phone at some point — a budget, a workout log, a small project tracker — and wished you could just *ask* it a question instead of squinting at the cells. That moment just got easier on iOS.

## What you can do with it

According to Google, Gemini in Sheets on iOS works much like the web and Android versions. You tap the Gemini **spark icon** inside a spreadsheet, and a chat panel opens. From there, you can:

- Ask plain-English questions about your data — think of a **prompt** (the instruction you type to an AI) like "Which category did I spend the most on last month?"
- Generate **analytical insights**, which is a fancy way of saying "have the AI spot patterns or trends you might miss."
- Create **charts** without manually selecting ranges and clicking through menus.

To lower the blank-page barrier, Google includes a couple of suggested prompts, such as *"Summarize this table"* and *"Analyze for insights"*, so you don't have to invent the perfect question right away.

The examples Google shared show this working on two everyday kinds of spreadsheets: a personal **Finance Tracker** and a small-team **Employee Tracker**. Both are the kind of thing many people already keep in Sheets.

## Who can use it

The feature is rolling out across several paid Google plans:

- **Workspace Business**: Starter, Standard, and Plus
- **Workspace Enterprise**: Starter, Standard, and Plus
- **Education**: the Google AI Pro for Education add-on
- **Consumer**: Google AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra

If you're on one of those plans and Gemini is already enabled for your account, you don't need to flip any switches — the feature shows up by default. Google notes there is no separate admin toggle for this mobile version beyond the general Gemini for Google Workspace setting.

## When you'll see it

Google says the gradual rollout started on **October 15, 2026**, and full visibility can take up to **15 days**. So if you don't see the icon on day one, give it a little time.

## What this means for you

- **If you work with data on the go**: this is the easiest way yet to check a number or pull a quick chart without booting up a laptop. Worth opening Sheets the next time you're stuck waiting in line.
- **If you manage personal finances or side projects**: the suggested prompts ("Summarize this table," "Analyze for insights") are a friendly starting point — you don't need to write detailed instructions.
- **If you're new to AI helpers**: think of Gemini as a chat-style assistant sitting next to your cells. You type a question, it reads the spreadsheet, and answers in plain English.
- **If you already use it**: try combining two requests in one prompt — for example, "Summarize this table and make a bar chart of the top three categories." It saves a round trip.

## Wrap-up

Gemini in Sheets on iOS turns your phone into a small data analyst — handy for quick questions, casual summaries, and the occasional chart when you're away from your desk. Open the Google Sheets app on your iPhone, look for the Gemini spark icon inside one of your spreadsheets, and try the suggested prompt that fits what you're working on.
